slides.0.title: Industry and market
slides.0.subtitle: Pays d'Oc IGP, cooperatives, bulk wine and crisis
slides.1.title: Pays d'Oc IGP
slides.1.highlights.0.title: History
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Created as Vin de Pays d'Oc in 1987 and converted to IGP Pays d'Oc on 1 August 2009 (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Scale
slides.1.highlights.1.content: About 120,000 ha across the Hérault, Aude, Gard and Pyrénées-Orientales; 6.8 million hL in 2021; 58 varieties permitted (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Varietal labelling
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Naming a variety on an IGP requires at least 85% of it; vintage may be stated on all IGPs (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.content: Pays d'Oc is France's most successful varietal IGP and the engine of Languedoc exports.
slides.2.title: The IGP system
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Vin de Pays renamed
slides.2.highlights.0.content: All Vin de Pays were renamed IGP on 1 August 2009 under Regulation 607/2009, and 150-plus titles became 75 IGP zones (Wine With Seth); the legislation date (1973 or 1979) is given inconsistently
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Three levels
slides.2.highlights.1.content: 75 IGPs = 6 regional + 28 departmental + 41 petites zones (Wine With Seth); Pays d'Oc is a regional IGP
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Vin de France
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The base level below IGP; it can blend across regions and may generally state variety and vintage (after the 2009 EU reform)
slides.2.content: IGP freedom is commercial flexibility and also a challenge for signalling quality.
slides.3.title: Cooperatives and scale
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Sieur d'Arques
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The Limoux cooperative grew from 350,000 to 6.5 million bottles a year between 1960 and 1985 (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Small and cooperative together
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Terrasses du Larzac has 3 cooperatives, about 90 private estates and 3 merchants (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Ageing growers
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Pleinchamp (2024): one farmer in three in the Pyrénées-Orientales is over 60
slides.3.content: Cooperative scale gives steady supply and also transmits price pressure.
slides.4.title: Crisis and vine-pull
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Definitive vine-pull
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Pleinchamp (8 Nov 2024): up to €4,000/ha with a €120 million budget cap; Languedoc-Roussillon is about a quarter of national vineyard area but more than half of preliminary applications
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Demand
slides.4.highlights.1.content: The trade expects domestic consumption to fall 20% over the next decade; France distilled 10% of its 2023 harvest; Bordeaux is removing about 8,000 ha
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Exports
slides.4.highlights.2.content: A Le Journal des Entreprises headline says Languedoc wine exports fell 6% in 2024 (full text not retrieved; cited as a headline only and not tested)
slides.4.content: The crisis comes from climate (supply) and consumption (demand), and vine-pull addresses only one end.
